papers.title: Scout Before You Route: Predicting Task Success and Token Count from a Small LLM Prefill
papers.abstract: Routers typically choose a model per query by trading predicted correctness against cost. Most price each model at a fixed cost, as if every query used the same number of output tokens, but the output length of reasoning models varies by an order of magnitude across queries. When is per-query cost worth predicting? What factors drive cost? How cheaply can predictions be made? We predict both the success probability and the output length of candidate models from the prefill activations of a single small frozen LLM, the scout. With reasoning candidates, perfect per-query cost knowledge would save 29-61% of spending on eight of nine datasets, and much less with non-reasoning candidates on the same problems. On those eight datasets, our predicted costs save 9-33% at matched accuracy relative to median-length pricing, up to 69% of what perfect knowledge would save. They are significantly cheaper than each estimator we reimplemented or adapted from published work, including ZeroRouter and a MixLLM-style predictor, on a majority of datasets. Output length depends mostly on the problem. On most math and code datasets, harder problems are longer, so predicted success alone prices cost nearly as well. On knowledge and mixed-format datasets they are not, and predicted success falls well behind a probe trained on length. The probe keeps most of its saving with 20 labelled problems and transfers without labels to four of seven new benchmarks. On a mixture of all nine benchmarks, it saves 22% beyond pricing each benchmark at its own median length. Savings stop growing at about a 2B scout, so above 4B a larger scout costs more than it adds.

papers.title: "Despite her age, Margaret was eager to make a change": Unpacking Aging Representations and Stereotypes in LLM-generated Stories
papers.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) increasingly generate everyday stories, their portrayals can shape expectations about aging. Prior work has largely examined age stereotypes in short responses, leaving unanswered whose lives models default to imagining and how age shapes characters' roles in complete narratives. We analyze 594 stories generated by Gemini, GPT, and Llama using text embeddings, LLM-assisted coding, and qualitative analysis. When age was unspecified, stories typically featured younger adults, with middle-aged protagonists largely absent. Older adults were often portrayed through loss, familiar routines, and help from younger characters. Even positive stories sometimes treated older adults' achievements as surprising or portrayed others making decisions on their behalf. We suggest evaluating not only the tone of generated stories, but also who appears, what opportunities they receive, and who makes decisions. Involving older adults in these evaluations can guide writing tools toward more varied, less stereotyped portrayals of later life.

translation.title: "Despite her age, Margaret was eager to make a change": Unpacking Aging Representations and Stereotypes in LLM-generated Stories
translation.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) increasingly generate everyday stories, their portrayals can shape expectations about aging. Prior work has largely examined age stereotypes in short responses, leaving unanswered whose lives models default to imagining and how age shapes characters' roles in complete narratives. We analyze 594 stories generated by Gemini, GPT, and Llama using text embeddings, LLM-assisted coding, and qualitative analysis. When age was unspecified, stories typically featured younger adults, with middle-aged protagonists largely absent. Older adults were often portrayed through loss, familiar routines, and help from younger characters. Even positive stories sometimes treated older adults' achievements as surprising or portrayed others making decisions on their behalf. We suggest evaluating not only the tone of generated stories, but also who appears, what opportunities they receive, and who makes decisions. Involving older adults in these evaluations can guide writing tools toward more varied, less stereotyped portrayals of later life.

papers.title: Grounding-Aware Judge Reward Reinforcement Learning for Out-of-Domain Face Anti-Spoofing
papers.abstract: Face Anti-Spoofing (FAS) must distinguish genuine faces from presentation attacks. A unified Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM) is an attractive solution: it detects physical attacks (print, replay, mask) in one model and produces interpretable forensic evidence via Chain-of-Thought (CoT). A central obstacle to post-training such a model with reinforcement learning is that FAS reasoning has no rule-verifiable ground truth: only the binary verdict is checkable, while the reasoning chain cannot be verified by any hand-crafted rule. Optimizing the verdict alone is therefore a sparse, hackable signal. The model can reach the correct answer through a shortcut such as a false-rejection bias, which does not generalize. We address this with a grounding-aware judge reward. A 32B vision-language judge scores each reasoning chain against the image on evidence anchoring, logical coherence, and domain knowledge, turning the image itself into the verification signal. The reward is applied in a Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) stage after CoT supervised fine-tuning. It is the judge, rather than the RL objective, that supplies the process supervision a verdict-only reward cannot. Our study starts from a model that already performs well In-Domain (ID) after CoT-based supervised fine-tuning and asks how to improve its Out-of-Domain (OOD) generalization. We find that grounding-aware rewards are an effective means to that end. We validate the method on OOD generalization, where the reward reduces ACER on two physical benchmarks (LCC-FASD 0.288 to 0.273, MSU-MFSD 0.431 to 0.409) while preserving ID accuracy (CelebA-Spoof 0.033 to 0.035). Against ResNet-50/101 and CLIP-ViT-B/16 baselines, the MLLM dominates ID and matches or surpasses the strongest baseline OOD. To our knowledge this is the first use of LLM-as-judge process supervision for FAS.

papers.title: LeanDojo-v2: A Comprehensive Library for AI-Assisted Theorem Proving in Lean
papers.abstract: Building on recent progress in machine learning for formal theorem proving in Lean, we introduce LeanDojo-v2: an end-to-end framework that unifies repository data extraction, LLM fine-tuning, proof search, AI autocompletion, and LLM-assisted theorem proving in a single software library. In addition, we provide Lean4Code, a lightweight IDE that integrates the various features of LeanDojo-v2 through a simple, mathematician-friendly UI. These tools will enable mathematicians and researchers to easily fine-tune language models on domain-specific Lean codebases and experiment with LLM-assisted theorem proving without a complex setup.

translation.title: LeanDojo-v2：一个用于 Lean 中 AI 辅助定理证明的综合库
translation.abstract: 基于机器学习在 Lean 形式化定理证明方面的最新进展，我们提出 LeanDojo-v2：一个端到端框架，将仓库数据提取、LLM 微调、证明搜索、AI 自动补全和 LLM 辅助定理证明统一在同一个软件库中。此外，我们提供 Lean4Code，一个轻量级 IDE，通过简洁、对数学家友好的 UI 集成了 LeanDojo-v2 的各项功能。这些工具将使数学家和研究人员能够轻松地在特定领域的 Lean 代码库上微调语言模型，并在无需复杂配置的情况下实验 LLM 辅助定理证明。
translation.brief: 解决在 Lean 中进行 AI 辅助定理证明需要复杂工具链的问题，核心方法是构建一个统一数据提取、微调、证明搜索与 IDE 的端到端软件库。

papers.title: From Emergence to Reversibility: Toward Reversible Multi-Agent Systems
papers.abstract: Multi-agent systems become capable through institutional mechanisms, such as rules that route information to agents that act on it. These mechanisms are also natural places to restrict the system. Yet as agents learn, share memory, delegate, and repair failures, the collective can find other paths to the same effects: a restriction on the original mechanism still operates but no longer stops them, while routine performance and compliance checks pass. We propose \textbf{Reversible Multi-agent Systems} as a research agenda: collectives that grow while an authorized supervisor can still restrict specified effects, keep them restricted as agents adapt, and reconstitute useful cooperation under renewed authority. What is reversed is the ability to produce a specified effect; restrictions must hold even if learned knowledge persists. The goal is to preserve effective intervention, not a particular mechanism: at every step of growth, some authorized intervention must keep a specified prohibited effect rare while maintaining required service. We identify three research problems: tracking what capabilities depend on, handing off control before an old mechanism loses its effect, and separating legitimate repair from unauthorized reconstruction. We outline how to evaluate control across growth paths, back control claims with evidence, and allocate the rights to restrict and restore.

translation.title: 从涌现到可逆性：迈向可逆多智能体系统
translation.abstract: 多智能体系统通过制度性机制（如将信息路由给执行智能体的规则）获得能力，而这些机制也是限制系统的自然位置。然而随着智能体学习、共享记忆、委托和修复故障，集体可以找到通往相同效果的其他路径：对原始机制的限制仍然生效，但不再能阻止它们，而常规运行和合规检查依然通过。我们提出可逆多智能体系统作为研究议程：集体在增长的同时，授权监督者仍能限制特定效果，在智能体适应后保持限制，并在恢复授权后重建有用的合作。被逆转的是产生特定效果的能力；即使学到的知识仍然存在，限制也必须成立。目标是保留有效干预，而非特定机制：在增长的每一步，都必须存在某种授权干预，使特定的禁止效果保持罕见，同时维持所需服务。我们识别出三个研究问题：追踪能力依赖于什么、在旧机制失效前移交控制、以及区分合法修复与未授权重建。我们概述了如何在增长路径上评估控制、用证据支撑控制声明，以及分配限制与恢复的权利。
translation.brief: 解决多智能体系统在学习和适应后绕过原有机制限制的问题，核心方法是提出可逆多智能体系统研究议程，保证授权干预在系统增长全程持续有效。

papers.title: Real-Time Short-Response Selection for Spoken Dialogue Systems
papers.abstract: To realize spoken dialogue systems that can interact naturally with users, it is important for the system to respond to user utterances at appropriate timings. To achieve such natural turn-taking, the system needs not only to predict appropriate response timings but also to mask delays caused by language generation and speech synthesis so that they are not perceived by the user. We propose a real-time short-response selection task that can be integrated with existing turn-taking models to mask generation delay. To address this task, the proposed model learns the mapping between dialogue context and short responses using contrastive learning. When a turn-taking event is detected, the system selects a response from a set of pre-generated candidates. The selected response is played while the main response is being generated. Experimental results show that the proposed method learns to select short responses based on dialogue context, outperforming random and LLM-based baselines. Moreover, integrating response selection maintained turn-taking prediction performance and added minimal processing overhead.

translation.title: 面向口语对话系统的实时短响应选择
translation.abstract: 为实现能与用户自然交互的口语对话系统，系统在恰当的时机响应用户话语非常重要。为实现这种自然的轮次转换，系统不仅需要预测合适的响应时机，还需要掩盖语言生成和语音合成造成的延迟，使其不被用户感知。我们提出一个可与现有轮次转换模型集成的实时短响应选择任务，用于掩盖生成延迟。为解决该任务，所提出的模型使用对比学习来学习对话上下文与短响应之间的映射。当检测到轮次转换事件时，系统从一组预生成的候选响应中选择一个，并在主响应生成期间播放。实验结果表明，所提方法学会基于对话上下文选择短响应，优于随机和基于 LLM 的基线。此外，集成响应选择保持了轮次转换预测性能，且处理开销极小。
translation.brief: 解决对话系统生成延迟被用户感知的问题，核心方法是用对比学习实时从预生成候选中选择短响应来填补等待时间。

papers.title: Fair Selection of Generalized Nash Equilibria: A Comparability Perspective
papers.abstract: Generalized Nash equilibrium (GNE) problems model self-interested agents coupled through their costs and shared constraints, and arise throughout control applications that allocate a scarce common resource. Such problems typically admit a continuum of equilibria, so any implementation must \emph{select} one. This selection is not neutral: it decides how the cost of the shared constraint is distributed among the agents, a decision often expected to be fair. The variational GNE (v-GNE), which charges all agents a uniform shadow price, is the conventional choice and is frequently advocated as fair. Through the lens of \emph{comparability} from social choice theory, we show that the GNE set itself requires no inter-agent comparability of costs, whereas the v-GNE implicitly assumes cardinal unit comparability, one of the stronger notions. We then introduce the fair GNE (f-GNE), which selects an equilibrium by explicitly optimizing a fairness metric matched to the comparability at hand, and give constructive routes to compute it for single-constraint and linear-quadratic games. An electric-vehicle charging game serves as a running example throughout this self-contained tutorial.

translation.title: 广义纳什均衡的公平选择：可比较性视角
translation.abstract: 广义纳什均衡（GNE）问题建模通过成本和共享约束耦合的自利智能体，广泛出现在分配稀缺公共资源的控制应用中。此类问题通常存在连续统的均衡，因此任何实现都必须选择其中一个。这种选择并非中立：它决定了共享约束的成本如何在智能体之间分配，而这一决策通常被期望是公平的。变分 GNE（v-GNE）向所有智能体收取统一的影子价格，是传统选择并常被倡导为公平的。通过社会选择理论中可比较性的视角，我们表明 GNE 集本身不需要智能体间成本的可比较性，而 v-GNE 隐含假设了基数单位可比较性——这是较强的概念之一。我们随后提出公平 GNE（f-GNE），通过显式优化与当前可比较性相匹配的公平性指标来选择均衡，并给出在单约束和线性二次博弈中计算它的构造性方法。一个电动汽车充电博弈作为贯穿本自足教程的运行示例。
translation.brief: 解决 GNE 均衡选择中成本分配公平性被忽视的问题，核心方法是基于社会选择理论的可比较性提出显式优化公平指标的 f-GNE。

papers.title: Does Reasoning Improve Psychological Depth in Large Language Models?
papers.abstract: Benchmark gains from reasoning-enhanced large language models encourage the assumption that these models should broadly perform better on complex generative tasks, but this remains underexplored in open-ended, creative domains shaped by nuances of reader experience. We tested this assumption through the lens of psychological depth in short stories. We compared DeepSeek-R1 vs. DeepSeek-V3, our closest available contrast for reasoning-oriented post-training, and GPT-5 vs. GPT-4o, through 60 blinded pairwise evaluations in which seven human annotators and an ensemble LLM-as-a-Judge rated prompt-matched story outputs. Human evaluations showed no universal reasoning advantage: GPT-5 was slightly preferred over GPT-4o (60.0-62.9% across two reasoning-effort settings), whereas DeepSeek-R1 fell behind DeepSeek-V3 (42.9%). Although this pattern was marked by low inter-annotator agreement (Krippendorff's $\alpha = 0.070$), our annotation-quality checks suggested genuine evaluative subjectivity, plausibly reflecting distinct annotator decision schemes rather than annotation failure. In contrast, the LLM-as-a-Judge showed a strong pro-reasoning bias (98.3% of pairs vs. 55.2% of human votes), consistent across its five configurations and partly tracking sentence length. These findings suggest that, at the frontier, reasoning-related quality differences are small enough to be dominated by reader subjectivity, and that LLM-as-a-Judge evaluators can obscure this subjectivity in nuanced creative-generation tasks.

translation.title: 推理能力能否提升大语言模型的心理深度？
translation.abstract: 推理增强型大语言模型在基准测试上的提升让人假设这些模型在复杂生成任务上应普遍表现更好，但这在受读者体验细微差别影响的开放式创意领域仍未被充分探索。我们通过短篇小说的心理深度来检验这一假设。我们比较了 DeepSeek-R1 与 DeepSeek-V3（最接近的推理导向后训练对比）以及 GPT-5 与 GPT-4o，进行了 60 次盲测成对评估，由七位人类标注者和一个 LLM-as-a-Judge 集成对提示匹配的故事输出进行评分。人类评估未显示推理的普遍优势：GPT-5 略优于 GPT-4o（两种推理努力设置下为 60.0-62.9%），而 DeepSeek-R1 落后于 DeepSeek-V3（42.9%）。尽管这一模式伴随较低的标注者间一致性（Krippendorff's α = 0.070），我们的标注质量检查表明这是真实的评价主观性，可能反映了标注者不同的决策方案而非标注失败。相比之下，LLM-as-a-Judge 表现出强烈的亲推理偏差（98.3% 的成对 vs. 人类投票的 55.2%），在其五种配置中一致，并部分与句子长度相关。这些发现表明，在前沿水平上，推理相关的质量差异小到会被读者主观性所主导，而 LLM-as-a-Judge 评估者可能在细腻的创意生成任务中掩盖这种主观性。
translation.brief: 检验推理增强 LLM 是否在创意写作的心理深度上更优，核心方法是通过人类与 LLM 评委的盲测成对评估比较推理与非推理模型。

papers.title: MongoBench: Do LLMs Know What a MongoDB Query Will Do?
papers.abstract: LLM agents increasingly operate databases on their own: they generate queries and run them against live data. Two checks are commonly used to judge such an agent - whether it produces a valid query, and whether it reaches the right final answer - but neither tells us whether the agent knows what its query will actually do before it runs. We argue that this consequence prediction ability must be evaluated in its own right, and we build MongoBench to measure it: given a collection of documents and a MongoDB find() filter, a model must return the exact set of matching _ids, with ground truth from a real mongod server. The 300 items each compose three or four documented matching pitfalls and are proposed symmetrically by three vendors' models, so results stratify by item source. Evaluating four models - frontier systems from three vendors and one open-weight reasoner - accuracy ranges from 70.1% to 92.1%, a 22-point spread. Each proposer mispredicts 10-31% of the items it wrote itself, so producing a query does not imply predicting its effect. A failure-mode analysis shows errors are better predicted by which semantic pitfall a query exercises - range comparisons and null - than by surface measures such as document count or the number of composed rules. Prepending a verified rule sheet helps unevenly; executing the original filter against the engine yields reliable match sets, but delegation must be checked: on 28% of items (averaged over three runs) one model's executed filters never passed a canonical check against the intended query, and it answered about 22 of them wrong, while the other three passed on every item. We release the benchmark, the mongod oracle, and the evaluation code with all prompts at this https URL.

translation.title: MongoBench：LLM 真的了解 MongoDB 查询会产生什么效果吗？
translation.abstract: LLM 智能体越来越多地自主操作数据库：它们生成查询并对真实数据执行。目前常用两种检查来评判这类智能体——是否生成有效查询、是否得到正确的最终答案——但两者都无法说明智能体在执行前是否知道查询会实际产生什么效果。我们认为这种后果预测能力必须被独立评估，为此构建了 MongoBench 来衡量它：给定一个文档集合和一个 MongoDB find() 过滤器，模型必须返回精确匹配的 _id 集合，真值来自真实的 mongod 服务器。300 个测试项各自组合了三到四个有文档记载的匹配陷阱，并由三家厂商的模型对称提出，因此结果可按测试项来源分层。对四个模型——三家厂商的前沿系统和一个开放权重推理模型——的评估显示，准确率介于 70.1% 到 92.1% 之间，相差 22 个百分点。每个提出者对自己编写的测试项也有 10-31% 预测错误，说明能生成查询并不意味着能预测其效果。失败模式分析表明，错误更能由查询涉及哪类语义陷阱——范围比较和 null——来预测，而非文档数量或组合规则数等表面指标。在提示前附加经验证的规则表帮助不均衡；将原始过滤器交给引擎执行能得到可靠的匹配集合，但委托必须被检查：在 28% 的测试项上（三次运行平均），一个模型执行的过滤器从未通过与预期查询的规范校验，其中约 22 个它答错了，而其他三个模型在所有测试项上都通过了。我们在 https URL 发布了基准、mongod oracle 和包含所有提示的评估代码。
translation.brief: 针对 LLM 无法预测其 MongoDB 查询实际效果的问题，构建了要求模型精确返回匹配 _id 集合的 MongoBench 基准来独立评估后果预测能力。

papers.title: Large Language Model Deployment on Resource-Constrained Edge Devices: A Practitioners Survey
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have transformed many areas of artificial intelligence (AI), but their substantial resource requirements limit their deployment on mobile and edge devices. Although LLMs have demonstrated impressive capabilities in various applications, the next challenge is deploying these models on resource-limited edge devices. Recent innovations in software optimizations and specialized hardware have made it feasible to deploy LLMs on edge devices. Edge deployment offers benefits including local data processing, cost savings, reduced latency, and personalized responses. This paper reviews the latest techniques that make the deployment of LLMs on edge devices feasible.

translation.title: 大语言模型在资源受限边缘设备上的部署：从业者综述
translation.abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）已经变革了人工智能（AI）的许多领域，但其巨大的资源需求限制了它们在移动和边缘设备上的部署。尽管 LLM 在各种应用中展现了令人印象深刻的能力，下一个挑战是将这些模型部署到资源受限的边缘设备上。软件优化和专用硬件方面的最新创新使得在边缘设备上部署 LLM 成为可能。边缘部署带来诸多好处，包括本地数据处理、成本节约、降低延迟和个性化响应。本文综述了使 LLM 在边缘设备上部署成为可能的最新技术。
translation.brief: 综述使 LLM 能够部署在资源受限边缘设备上的最新软件优化与专用硬件技术。

papers.title: The Invisible Gap: Romanized Indic Generation Fails Where Automatic Metrics Succeed
papers.abstract: Hundreds of millions of Indians communicate with digital systems in romanized Latin characters -- typing "aap kaise hain" rather than native script -- yet romanized Indic generation is absent from NLP benchmarks and evaluation frameworks. We demonstrate that automatic metrics (BGE-M3, BERTScore) systematically misrepresent the quality of romanized Hindi, Telugu, and Kannada generation. We evaluate four LLMs (Claude Opus 4.8, GPT-5.5, Gemini 2.5-flash, Qwen3.5-35B) on 142 OpenAssistant query-response pairs. On a 72-response diagnostic subset, native speakers rate GPT-5.5 1.43 points higher than Claude Opus 4.8 on a 12-point rubric, whereas their full-dataset BGE-M3 means differ by only 0.004. Two distinct model-specific failure modes emerge: Gemini produces script spillage (16.9% of Telugu responses leak native script), while Qwen collapses to English-only output (16.2% of Kannada responses). We introduce a failure-aware evaluation policy that assigns zero to empty outputs, script-corrupted responses, and instruction collapses -- revealing failures metrics alone cannot detect. Our results show that evaluating romanized Indic generation requires a coordinated bundle: semantic similarity, script compliance, failure coverage, and native-speaker acceptability.

translation.title: 看不见的鸿沟：罗马化印度语系生成在自动指标失效处失败
translation.abstract: 数以亿计的印度人使用罗马化拉丁字符与数字系统交流——输入 "aap kaise hain" 而非原生文字——然而罗马化印度语系生成在 NLP 基准和评估框架中却缺席。我们证明自动指标（BGE-M3、BERTScore）系统性地错误呈现罗马化印地语、泰卢固语和卡纳达语生成的质量。我们在 142 个 OpenAssistant 问答对上评估了四个 LLM（Claude Opus 4.8、GPT-5.5、Gemini 2.5-flash、Qwen3.5-35B）。在一个 72 条回复的诊断子集上，母语者按 12 分量表给 GPT-5.5 的评分比 Claude Opus 4.8 高 1.43 分，而两者在全数据集上的 BGE-M3 均值仅相差 0.004。出现了两种不同的模型特定失败模式：Gemini 产生文字溢出（16.9% 的泰卢固语回复泄漏原生文字），而 Qwen 坍缩为纯英文输出（16.2% 的卡纳达语回复）。我们引入一种失败感知的评估策略，对空输出、文字损坏的回复和指令坍缩赋零分——揭示出仅靠指标无法检测的失败。我们的结果表明，评估罗马化印度语系生成需要一个协调的组合：语义相似度、文字合规性、失败覆盖率和母语者可接受度。
translation.brief: 针对自动指标无法反映罗马化印度语系生成质量的问题，提出结合语义相似度、文字合规、失败覆盖与母语者评估的失败感知评估策略。

papers.title: When Routine Operations Break Architectural Pattern Relationships in LLM Agent Harnesses
papers.abstract: LLM agent harnesses distribute tool mediation, state management and safety guardrails across native services, independently written plugins and configuration. Routine operations can change the runtime order or retained state that architectural pattern relationships require, without any code change. We study five relationships associated with the Guardrail Enforcement Point, Autonomy Controller and Blackboard patterns across five released harnesses, analysing a main sample of fourteen independently written plugins. Using PatternOps, our assessment procedure, we trace requirements from pattern descriptions, provider documentation and deployment profiles to the providers that realise them and the records that decide them. We then compare alternative allocations under supported operations. Such operations broke relationships silently: after a plugin was reapplied or an allow rule saved, policy stopped evaluating edits while every plugin stayed active, and a prohibited edit executed. Which alternatives qualified depended on the requirement. Allocations that kept the required order, or kept or rebuilt the needed state, held on their tested paths and operation sequences, while others prevented prohibited effects but missed edits rejected elsewhere. In these harnesses, a pattern relationship is a property of the running system and its history, so architects should evaluate it against the decision paths, state lifetimes and operation sequences their deployments use.

translation.title: 当常规操作破坏 LLM 智能体框架中的架构模式关系时
translation.abstract: LLM 智能体框架将工具中介、状态管理和安全护栏分布在原生服务、独立编写的插件和配置之中。常规操作可以在不修改任何代码的情况下改变架构模式关系所要求的运行时顺序或保留状态。我们研究了五个已发布框架中与 Guardrail Enforcement Point、Autonomy Controller 和 Blackboard 模式相关的五种关系，分析了由十四个独立编写插件构成的主样本。使用我们的评估流程 PatternOps，我们将模式描述、提供商文档和部署配置中的需求追溯到实现它们的提供商以及决定它们的记录。然后我们比较受支持操作下的不同分配方案。这类操作会静默地破坏关系：在重新应用某个插件或保存一条 allow 规则后，策略停止了对编辑的评估，而所有插件仍保持活跃，一条被禁止的编辑得以执行。哪些备选方案合格取决于具体需求。保持所需顺序、或保留/重建所需状态的分配在其测试路径和操作序列上成立，而其他方案虽阻止了被禁止的效果，却遗漏了在别处被拒绝的编辑。在这些框架中，模式关系是运行系统及其历史的属性，因此架构师应针对其部署所使用的决策路径、状态生命周期和操作序列来评估它。
translation.brief: 研究常规运维操作如何在无代码改动的情况下静默破坏 LLM 智能体框架中的架构模式关系，并提出 PatternOps 评估流程来追溯和比较不同分配方案。

papers.title: MARS: Training Multilingual Search Agents for Retriever-Free Evidence Acquisition
papers.abstract: Existing multilingual retrieval-augmented generation relies heavily on learned retrievers and similarity-based ranking from multilingual collections, which are vulnerable to cross-lingual retrieval errors and indexing overhead. In this paper, we explore retriever-free multilingual search, where the model directly interacts with raw corpora through executable shell commands. This paradigm shifts the bottleneck to multilingual search action generation, where exact search is sensitive to entity surface forms and outcome-only supervision provides limited guidance for multi-turn search. To address these challenges, we propose MARS, a multilingual search agent in direct corpus interaction (DCI) with reinforcement learning (RL). MARS introduces corpus-native entity grounding to recover reliable lexical anchors from corpus evidence, mitigating failure to retrieve evidence. Meanwhile, we present a redundancy-aware search reward to encourage concise and effective search trajectories, addressing training collapse in RL of multilingual scenarios. Experiments show that \ours~consistently outperforms strong retrieval-based and DCI baselines, while demonstrating robust cross-lingual generalization and substantially reducing redundant corpus interactions.

translation.title: MARS：训练多语言搜索智能体以实现免检索器的证据获取
translation.abstract: 现有多语言检索增强生成严重依赖学习型检索器和基于相似度的多语言集合排序，这容易受到跨语言检索错误和索引开销的影响。本文探索免检索器的多语言搜索，模型通过可执行的 shell 命令直接与原始语料库交互。这一范式将瓶颈转移到多语言搜索动作生成上：精确搜索对实体的表层形式敏感，而仅基于结果的监督对多轮搜索提供的指导有限。为应对这些挑战，我们提出 MARS，一个通过强化学习（RL）在直接语料交互（DCI）中进行搜索的多语言搜索智能体。MARS 引入语料原生的实体 grounding，从语料证据中恢复可靠的词法锚点，缓解证据检索失败。同时，我们提出一种冗余感知的搜索奖励，鼓励简洁有效的搜索轨迹，解决多语言场景 RL 中的训练坍缩问题。实验表明，MARS 持续优于强大的基于检索和 DCI 的基线，同时展现出稳健的跨语言泛化能力，并大幅减少冗余的语料交互。
translation.brief: 针对多语言检索增强生成中跨语言检索错误和索引开销问题，提出通过强化学习训练直接与语料交互的搜索智能体 MARS，结合语料原生实体 grounding 和冗余感知奖励。

papers.title: AdaAlloc: Adaptive Visual Token Allocation for Long-Video Question Answering
papers.abstract: Long-video question answering forces multimodal large language models to reason under strict visual-token budgets, creating a tradeoff between broad temporal coverage and fine-grained spatial detail. Uniform sampling preserves coverage but often obscures decisive local cues, while caption-based or frame-similarity retrieval operates over lossy proxies that can miss motion, state changes, and before-after relations. We recast long-video reasoning as a visual-token allocation problem: given a fixed budget, decide how much to spend on global context versus high-resolution local evidence, and where in the video to draw that local evidence from. We introduce AdaAlloc, a training-free inference framework that adaptively allocates visual tokens between a global video overview and localized visual detail. AdaAlloc first plans a global/local allocation policy, then uses temporal grounding to locate candidate evidence segments and refines them into a compact temporal memory. The selected policy controls both frame sampling density and resolution, combining sparse, lower-resolution global frames with denser, higher-resolution local frames drawn from the refined memory. The final answerer reasons over the allocated global context and refined local evidence. Across LVBench, MLVU, VideoMME, and LongVideoBench, AdaAlloc improves over budget-matched uniform sampling by up to 10.5 percentage points and outperforms the compared frame-selection and agentic methods on their reported benchmarks.

papers.title: AlienBench: A Benchmark of Structural Novelty in Language Model Outputs
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for creative tasks such as writing, design, and idea generation. For these uses, it matters whether a model's ideas depart from familiar examples or stay close to them. Novelty is one standard measure of creativity, and current creativity evaluations ask human experts or LLM judges to rate how novel an output is. However, these ratings have no fixed reference for what counts as novel (or, in other terms, departure from the familiar). Measuring this departure requires a task with known familiar defaults. The structured imagination task from cognitive psychology is such a task. In this creativity test, people imagine a creature from another planet. The departure from features of Earth animals, such as bilateral symmetry and legs as mode of locomotion, is used as measure of creativity. We introduce AlienBench, a benchmark that adapts the structured imagination task to language models. Models describe alien creatures, and a panel of three LLM judges extracts ten biological features from the description and labels them as either Earth-typical or a departure. The sum of feature departures is the score of a description, from 0 to 10. Each model describes alien creatures under six prompt conditions that vary the framing of the task and the planetary environment. Each model generates 30 descriptions per condition (180 in total), and its overall score is the mean across these descriptions. We evaluate 10 language models, from frontier to open-weight models. Overall scores range from 3.28 (GPT-6 Luna) to 6.55 (Ministral 3 14B). Interestingly, open-weight models score higher than proprietary models in this task (5.40 vs. 4.58). Under the baseline prompt, the models depart from Earth defaults more often on average than 100 human participants on every feature. We release all prompts, generations, judge outputs, and scores.

papers.title: Trajectory Forcing: Exploiting Diffusion Trajectories for Autoregressive Long Video Generation
papers.abstract: Autoregressive (AR) modeling is arguably the only way to extend a fixed-length video diffusion model to longer or even streaming videos. However, existing AR diffusion methods use only the previously predicted chunk as context for the next, discarding the intermediate predictions that constitute the chunk's generation history. In contrast, conventional AR models such as LLMs condition on the entire history of preceding tokens. To this end, we propose Trajectory Forcing (TraF), an AR diffusion method that exploits the denoising trajectories of previous video chunks as context. TraF operates under two training regimes: (1) with ground-truth videos, where pseudo-trajectories are constructed from Gaussian interpolations and re-predicted by the model, and (2) with a teacher model, where real trajectories are obtained from the student's own denoising rollout. The first regime naturally provides a strong initialization for the second. On the 5-second VBench benchmark, TraF achieves a Total score of 85.15, outperforming Self Forcing (+0.84) and Causal Forcing (+1.11), with Quality and Semantic improving simultaneously. On 30-second generation---6$\times$ the training horizon---TraF achieves the highest overall quality among all compared methods.

papers.title: DARIC: A Position-Independent KV Cache Reuse System with Distribution-Aware Recomputation
papers.abstract: The context lengths of large language models (LLMs) are rapidly increasing in real-world applications such as agentic systems and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). To accelerate LLM inference in these scenarios, reusing position-independent key-value (KV) caches across requests has emerged as a promising approach. This technique typically relies on recomputing a selected subset of tokens to restore cross-chunk interactions. However, existing solutions suffer from critical limitations in both algorithmic efficiency and system deployment. Algorithmically, they overlook the distribution of KV cache deviations, leading to either high token-selection overhead or degraded generation quality. At the system level, the reliance on custom LLM execution flows for recomputation complicates deployment and prevents seamless integration with highly optimized inference engines. In this paper, we propose DARIC (\textbf{D}istribution-\textbf{A}ware \textbf{R}ecomputation for \textbf{I}ndependent KV \textbf{C}ache Reuse), a novel KV cache reuse method based on system-algorithm co-design. At its core, DARIC introduces a distribution-aware token selection strategy that adaptively schedules token recomputation based on empirical KV deviation patterns, striking an optimal balance between generation quality and computational efficiency. Moreover, DARIC is built on a lightweight system architecture that enables independent KV cache generation and recomputation with minimal integration overhead, fully preserving existing system-level optimizations of standard inference engines. Comprehensive experiments across various datasets and LLMs demonstrate that DARIC consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving a 1.1$\times$--4.5$\times$ speedup in time-to-first-token (TTFT) with negligible loss in generation quality. Code is available at this https URL.

papers.title: Authorization Drift in LLM Agents: Evaluating Boundary Compliance in Multi-Step Tool Use
papers.abstract: LLM agents can exceed their authorization boundaries while pursuing user goals without an adversary. We formalize this phenomenon as authorization drift across data, tool, scope, and time, and introduce the Authorization Drift Benchmark (ADB): 648 samples across seven domains, each pairing a sufficient compliant path with an attractive unauthorized shortcut. To ensure executable tasks, tempting shortcuts, and feasible compliant paths, Staged Execution-Reflective Synthesis (SERS) grounds benchmark validation in real agent rollouts rather than LLM self-critique. Across 13 LLMs and three frameworks (25,207 trajectories), greater capability accompanies greater drift, with frontier-capable models exhibiting drift rates of 0.43 to 0.61. Yet 86.18% of tasks admit an observed clean-success trajectory, showing that drift is avoidable. Drift is persistent and dominated by early data over-collection; apparent improvements under agentic scaffolds coincide with collapsing clean-completion performance. To understand potential harms to individuals and society, we map drift points to legal provisions across four jurisdictions, connecting overreach to privacy and information-security concerns. Data minimisation is the most frequently implicated provision, and 93.5% of legally grounded drifting runs map to multiple jurisdictions, making the potential consequences of authorization drift more interpretable.

papers.title: CARGO: Causal Attribution and Responsibility-Guided Preventive Safe Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Cooperative Driving
papers.abstract: This study presents Causal Attribution and Responsibility-Guided Optimization (CARGO), a multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for cooperative on-ramp merging in mixed traffic. A shared latent-context posterior and an action-conditioned response model estimate directed behavioral influence, with posterior uncertainty propagated into interaction-edge selection. Complementary attribution mechanisms couple signed influence with marginal team utility for cooperative reward shaping and assign responsibility from positive excess tail risk relative to a safe reference policy. Conditional diffusion generates future responses for action-dependent risk estimation. Responsibility-guided preventive optimization calibrates agent-specific risk-reduction requirements to local capacity within a policy trust region, using reserved safety margins, adaptive requirement scaling, and joint feasibility verification. Theoretical analysis establishes risk monotonicity and sufficient local conditions for non-decreasing environmental return under explicit assumptions. Experiments in highway-env across three traffic densities, together with controlled graph-recovery and attribution studies, support the effectiveness of the framework. Under high-density traffic, CARGO increases the success rate by 66.04\% and reduces the crash rate by 56.23\% relative to the best evaluated baseline for each metric.

papers.title: GreyZone: Production-quality Agentic Application Threats
papers.abstract: Agents are increasingly deployed across domains such as coding, banking, and commerce. Their ability to invoke tools and change application state makes security testing important for reliable deployment. Although agent security has been studied through various adversarial testing approaches, benchmarks grounded in production agent environments remain limited. We introduce GreyZone, a benchmark for evaluating automated red-teaming services against real-world agent applications. Unlike benchmarks such as AgentDojo, which primarily evaluate subject agents under attack, GreyZone evaluates services' ability to generate and deliver attacks that cause verified security-policy violations. We select independently developed, open-source agent applications with security boundaries concerning access permissions, confidentiality, and action authorization. These applications expose diverse attack surfaces, including those arising from multi-agent interactions and multimodal inputs. By grounding evaluation in application environments that preserve production-relevant workflows and independently verifying outcomes, GreyZone supports research on automated agent security testing. Specifically, we present two preliminary case studies using Promptfoo on Letta Code and Clawith to examine attack delivery, agent behavior, and verified outcomes. We release the benchmark, including subject agents and attack surfaces for each application, to support further research on agent testing methods.

papers.title: Rethinking Requirement-to-Code Traceability Through Single-Agent and Multi-Agent Approaches
papers.abstract: Requirements-to-code traceability supports essential software engineering activities, including change impact analysis, maintenance, and regulatory compliance. Existing approaches typically rely on a retrieval-and-classification pipeline, which suffers from an inherent retrieval bottleneck: relevant source files that are not retrieved cannot be recovered during subsequent analysis. In this paper, we revisit requirements-to-code traceability in light of the substantially larger context windows offered by modern large language models, which make repository-scale analysis feasible without a separate retrieval step. We propose three approaches: a single-agent approach that analyzes the entire code repository in one pass, and two multi-agent approaches based on self-verification and multi-agent debate. Our evaluation shows that the single-agent approach substantially improves recall, achieving 80.9%, a gain of 38.6 percentage points (pp) over the state-of-the-art retrieval-based baseline, albeit with a 25.8 pp reduction in precision. By leveraging collaborative reasoning, the multi-agent debate-based approach achieves the best overall precision-recall balance, with 24.5% precision and 71.0% recall, yielding an F2 score of 49.5%. This represents an improvement of 7.5 pp over the state of the art and 2.7 pp over the single-agent approach. While the quantitative evaluation establishes the overall effectiveness of the approaches, the aggregate metrics alone explain little due to the considerable variability across results. Importantly, qualitative analysis provides key insights into highly variable quantitative results: the retrieval approach suits requirements that echo the code's vocabulary; single-agent, full-context reasoning suits well-documented, consistently named code; and multi-agent debate suits indirect, conflicting, or distributed evidence.

papers.title: Analyzing Code Provenance in LLMs for Programming Education
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) play an increasing role in programming education, challenging traditional assessment methods as they can generate fully functional code instantly. This disrupts the reliability of student submissions as indicators of learning and effort. To address this issue, code provenance is essential for tracing the origins of code and distinguishing student-authored, AI-generated, and externally sourced components. We extend the Min-K% probability approach by incorporating synthetic non-member code generation and apply it to Python code for membership inference and provenance tracking. Evaluations cover free LLMs such as GPT-2, DistilGPT-2, and DialoGPT, as well as state-of-the-art commercial models including GPT-5, Gemini 2.5, Mistral, DeepSeek, and LLaMA 3.3. Before evaluating our approach on higher-education student assignments, we validate its feasibility using Stack Overflow data. The results show that free models enable more sensitive code memorization detection than commercial models. By systematically comparing these LLMs, we assess trade-offs between detection accuracy and privacy protection, taking an initial step toward effective assessment of AI-assisted programming education through combined provenance detection and process visibility.

papers.title: Large Language Model Consensus and Corpus-Adaptive Topic Modeling for Classifying and Mapping Patent Innovation
papers.abstract: Patent analytics increasingly relies on transformer representations and large language models (LLMs), yet linking conceptual classification, topic formation and interpretation requires explicit decisions about model roles and the evidence retained at each stage. In this design-oriented study, we propose and demonstrate a patent analytics pipeline that links these tasks and keeps each decision open to audit. Three LLMs separately classify each patent by novelty (radical or incremental) and innovation type (product, process, service). Radical and innovation-type labels each require two supporting votes, with Incremental used as the fallback novelty label. Topics are discovered by clustering PatentSBERTa embeddings, with parameter ranges scaled to corpus size. A patent-specific stopword list is applied only when topics are represented with class-based term frequency--inverse document frequency (c-TF-IDF), and a second embedding model supports inter-topic similarity, hierarchical refinement and visualization. An LLM then labels each topic from its ranked keywords and representative patents. We demonstrate the pipeline on 30,964 public-sector-related patents retrieved from this http URL. Across five category corpora ranging from 591 to 29,215 patents, the pipeline produced 74 category-specific topic instances with a macro-average document coverage of 98.1% and topic diversity of 0.900--1.000, and fewer than 1% of classification outputs returned UNKNOWN. Because every model vote and the evidence behind each topic label are retained, analysts can audit and revise the outputs. The demonstration establishes the feasibility and traceability of the pipeline; testing its labels against expert coding and benchmarking it against alternative pipelines are identified as the next steps. The pipeline offers a reusable basis for LLM-assisted patent analysis in technology intelligence.

papers.title: Copies Are Not Confirmations: How News Duplication Fools LLM Judges and Continual Learners
papers.abstract: Many news reports of a claim are copies of one source: wire stories, content shared within a media group, syndicated features and press releases. We ask whether LLM judges and continual learners treat such copies as independent confirmations. In 200,000 English CC-News articles, a MinHash detector links 18.9% to a near-copy from another outlet (precision 0.97 once boilerplate is removed); it links 92% of edited reprints to their originals but none of the LLM rewrites by phi4, Llama 3.2 or Gemini 2.5 Flash. Shown three identical reprints of a claim about an unknown person instead of one report, Llama 3.2 3B and phi4 14B raised the share of lies they accepted from 0.06 to 0.71 and from 0.21 to 0.90 and ignored a note that the reports came from one source; Gemini 2.5 Flash already believed a single report, and Gemini 2.5 Pro followed provenance notes and tables. In a simulated continual-learning stream, showing the judge one report per detected chain cut the copied lies it accepted by 0.10-0.24 across four judges, at a mean cost of no more than 4.2 percentage points of accepted truths. Against reworded copies, a test of how many of a report's named entities are absent from an earlier look-alike separates LLM rewrites from 100 labelled independent reports of the same event with AUC 0.98-0.99 and wrongly flags one; entity overlap alone does as well, TF-IDF and a current embedding model come close, and the test catches few natural same-source derivatives. With the miss patterns of generated rewrite networks, it cut the reworded-copy lies accepted from 0.67 to 0.20 (0.40 when the rewriter invents details). Counting reports or chains alone is not a reliable defence, the effect of provenance information depends on the judge, and colluding sources remain the open problem. Code and labels: this https URL

translation.title: 复制不等于证实：新闻重复如何欺骗 LLM 评判者与持续学习系统
translation.abstract: 关于某一说法的许多新闻报道其实是对同一来源的复制：通讯社稿件、媒体集团内共享的内容、辛迪加特稿和新闻通稿。我们研究 LLM 评判者与持续学习系统是否将这类复制视为独立证实。在 20 万篇英文 CC-News 文章中，一个 MinHash 检测器将 18.9% 的文章与另一媒体的近似副本关联起来（去除模板文字后精确率为 0.97）；它能将 92% 的编辑转载关联到原文，却无法关联 phi4、Llama 3.2 或 Gemini 2.5 Flash 的 LLM 改写版本。当向 Llama 3.2 3B 和 phi4 14B 展示关于某个陌生人的同一报道的三份完全相同的转载而非一份时，它们接受的谎言比例分别从 0.06 升至 0.71、从 0.21 升至 0.90，并且忽略了注明报道来自同一来源的提示；Gemini 2.5 Flash 本就相信单篇报道，而 Gemini 2.5 Pro 则遵循来源提示和表格。在模拟的持续学习数据流中，让评判者对每个检测到的复制链只看一篇报道，可将四个评判者接受的复制谎言减少 0.10-0.24，平均代价不超过 4.2 个百分点的被接受真话。针对改写副本，一种检测报道中多少命名实体在早前相似报道中缺失的测试，能以 AUC 0.98-0.99 将 LLM 改写与 100 篇标注的同一事件独立报道区分开，仅误报一篇；仅用实体重叠效果相当，TF-IDF 和当前嵌入模型接近，而该测试很少误伤自然的同源衍生报道。结合生成改写网络的漏检模式，它将接受的改写副本谎言从 0.67 降至 0.20（当改写者编造细节时为 0.40）。仅统计报道数或复制链数并非可靠防御，来源信息的效果取决于评判者，而串通来源仍是未解决的问题。代码与标注：this https URL
translation.brief: 研究新闻复制被 LLM 误当作独立证实的问题，提出基于 MinHash 复制链检测和实体缺失测试的去重防御方法。

papers.title: RPEG: Training Reasoning Language Models Scalably and Cost-Effectively
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) is now central to training Reasoning Language Models (RLMs), but RLM pipelines are difficult to scale and costly to run because each RL step couples multiple large models, heterogeneous stages, cross-step state, and complex asynchronous dependencies. Existing systems typically optimize only parts of this design space. We address this complexity by jointly optimizing the pipeline structure as well as its execution using a novel data-centric graph intermediate representation called RLM Pipeline Execution Graph (RPEG). RPEG exposes structural choices such as bounded asynchrony and actor-critic sharing together with execution optimizations such as stage fusion, fine-grained scheduling, and multi-dimensional model parallelism. It is coupled with a comprehensive analytical performance model for RLM training, jointly capturing compute, communication, memory, and hierarchical rack-, node-, and GPU-level effects. Across systems with up to 256 GH200 GPUs, our distributed runtime engine implementing RPEG improves performance by up to 2x over ReaL and reduces step latency by up to 2.48x over verl, while increasing hardware utilization by up to 30%. Overall, RPEG provides a graph-driven foundation for next-generation training pipelines for frontier reasoning LLMs.

translation.title: RPEG：可扩展且高性价比地训练推理语言模型
translation.abstract: 强化学习（RL）如今是训练推理语言模型（RLM）的核心手段，但 RLM 流水线难以扩展且运行成本高昂，因为每个 RL 步骤耦合了多个大模型、异构阶段、跨步骤状态和复杂的异步依赖。现有系统通常只优化该设计空间的一部分。我们通过一种名为 RLM Pipeline Execution Graph（RPEG）的新型以数据为中心的图中间表示，联合优化流水线结构及其执行来解决这一复杂性。RPEG 同时暴露结构性选择（如有界异步、actor-critic 共享）和执行优化（如阶段融合、细粒度调度、多维模型并行），并配套一个全面的 RLM 训练分析性能模型，联合刻画计算、通信、内存以及机架、节点和 GPU 层级的层次化效应。在多达 256 块 GH200 GPU 的系统上，实现 RPEG 的分布式运行时引擎相比 ReaL 性能提升最高 2 倍，相比 verl 步骤延迟降低最高 2.48 倍，同时硬件利用率提升最高 30%。总体而言，RPEG 为前沿推理 LLM 的下一代训练流水线提供了图驱动的基础。
translation.brief: 针对 RLM 强化学习训练流水线难以扩展且昂贵的问题，提出图中间表示 RPEG 联合优化流水线结构与执行。

papers.title: On the Limits of Execution Traces for Repairing Assertion Failures in LLM-Generated Code
papers.abstract: Iterative repair returns a failed program's error to a large language model (LLM) and asks it to fix it. After iterative repair, the remaining failures are mostly assertion failures: with four Qwen2.5 models, they make up 79% of residual failures on BigCodeBench, all on HumanEval and 93% on LiveCodeBench. We argue, through an information view of the feedback, that an assertion failure says little about where the fault lies. We propose Breakpoint Debugging (BPD), which returns the failed program annotated inline with its variables' runtime values. We take the tasks that iterative repair failed to fix with five repair attempts and compare two ways of spending five further generations on them: BPD, and resampling. On BigCodeBench, BPD repairs 26.7% of these tasks against 22.4%, and its advantage grows with model size. On HumanEval, BPD outperforms resampling but only slightly, and on LiveCodeBench, fresh sampling repairs more (6.5% against 4.9%). Furthermore, BPD reduces unchanged-code resubmissions from 28% to 8% on BigCodeBench. Using only the first failing test's trace, it outperforms tracing all failing tests while using fewer tokens than both all-trace BPD and plain iterative repair. On LiveCodeBench, BPD gives no gain even on the public tests, so a visible failing input is not enough for a trace to help. These results match the information view: a trace helps only when the test exposes a failing input, and the fault is an implementation slip; otherwise, a repair loop should resample rather than trace.

translation.title: 论执行轨迹在修复 LLM 生成代码断言失败中的局限
translation.abstract: 迭代修复将失败程序的错误信息返回给大语言模型（LLM）并要求其修复。经过迭代修复后，剩余失败大多是断言失败：使用四个 Qwen2.5 模型，它们在 BigCodeBench 上占残余失败的 79%，在 HumanEval 上占全部，在 LiveCodeBench 上占 93%。我们通过反馈的信息论视角论证，断言失败几乎不能说明故障所在。我们提出断点调试（BPD），将失败程序连同其变量运行时值的内联标注一起返回给模型。我们取迭代修复经五次尝试仍未能修复的任务，比较两种再花五次生成的方式：BPD 与重采样。在 BigCodeBench 上，BPD 修复了其中 26.7% 的任务，而重采样为 22.4%，且其优势随模型规模增大。在 HumanEval 上，BPD 仅略优于重采样；在 LiveCodeBench 上，重新采样修复得更多（6.5% 对 4.9%）。此外，BPD 将 BigCodeBench 上未改动代码的重复提交从 28% 降至 8%。仅使用首个失败测试的轨迹，其表现优于追踪所有失败测试，且 token 消耗少于全轨迹 BPD 和普通迭代修复。在 LiveCodeBench 上，即使对公开测试 BPD 也无增益，说明仅有一个可见的失败输入不足以让轨迹发挥作用。这些结果与信息论视角一致：只有当测试暴露了失败输入且故障是实现失误时，轨迹才有帮助；否则修复循环应重新采样而非追踪。
translation.brief: 针对 LLM 生成代码中断言失败难以修复的问题，提出将变量运行时值内联标注返回的断点调试方法，并分析其适用条件。

papers.title: BOXBOX: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement for Long-Running Performance Optimization
papers.abstract: Automated harness optimization improves agents by learning from trajectories and task feedback. Existing offline methods use reference answers to optimize harnesses for reuse on held-out tasks. However, many real-world tasks are open-ended, while long runs expose new difficulties that offline-optimized harnesses may not address. To study harness optimization in these settings, we introduce PerfRace, a benchmark for long-running performance optimization of software projects, and investigate whether agents can use task-specific experience to recursively improve their harnesses during an ongoing task. To this end, we introduce BOXBOX, which enables agent-triggered harness revision and kernel-managed hot reloading while preserving execution context. We evaluate BOXBOX on PerfRace under matched test-time budgets, comparing it with Frozen Harness, offline Harness Evolution, and Harness Scaling. BOXBOX achieves higher speedup with more efficient use of task time and model cost, reaching a Speedup@4h of 1.70x, compared with 1.54x for the strongest baseline.

translation.title: BOXBOX：面向长时间运行性能优化的递归式 Harness 自我改进
translation.abstract: 自动化 harness 优化通过学习轨迹和任务反馈来改进智能体。现有离线方法利用参考答案优化 harness 以便在留出任务上复用。然而许多现实任务是无终止的开放式任务，而长时间运行会暴露离线优化的 harness 可能无法应对的新困难。为研究这些场景下的 harness 优化，我们提出 PerfRace——一个面向软件项目长时间运行性能优化的基准，并研究智能体能否在任务进行中利用任务特定经验递归改进其 harness。为此，我们提出 BOXBOX，它支持智能体触发的 harness 修订和内核管理的热重载，同时保留执行上下文。在相同测试时预算下，我们在 PerfRace 上将 BOXBOX 与 Frozen Harness、离线 Harness Evolution 和 Harness Scaling 进行比较。BOXBOX 以更高效的任务时间和模型成本使用获得更高加速，Speedup@4h 达 1.70 倍，而最强基线为 1.54 倍。
translation.brief: 针对开放式长时任务中离线优化 harness 失效的问题，提出支持智能体触发修订与热重载的递归式 harness 自我改进系统 BOXBOX。

papers.title: Khmer PFGen-Bench: Building a Judge-Free Benchmark for Open-Ended Generation in a Low-Resource Language
papers.abstract: Benchmarks for open-ended generation often rely on large language model (LLM) judges, whose reliability in low-resource languages is uncertain. We introduce Khmer PFGen-Bench, to our knowledge the first judge-free benchmark for multi-sentence answers to questions composed directly in Khmer, a low-resource language. Khmer PFGen-Bench adapts the scorer of PFGen-Bench, a benchmark for Japanese that scores responses with keyword rules and n-gram statistics from LLM-generated references. This scoring requires references that are both valid and varied, which LLMs may not produce in Khmer, so we examine how to build such references. We find that post-trained models can give more valid but less varied references than their base variants, and that mixing model families increases variety for the same number of references. Using references from post-trained models in nine families, the benchmark yields model rankings that are stable across reference sets and consistent with a native speaker's ratings. These findings offer guidance for building judge-free benchmarks in other low-resource languages.

translation.title: Khmer PFGen-Bench：为低资源语言的开放式生成构建无需评判模型的基准
translation.abstract: 开放式生成基准通常依赖大语言模型（LLM）评判者，而其在低资源语言中的可靠性尚不确定。我们提出 Khmer PFGen-Bench，据我们所知是首个针对直接以高棉语（一种低资源语言）撰写的问题的多句回答的无评判基准。Khmer PFGen-Bench 改编自面向日语的 PFGen-Bench 的评分器，后者使用关键词规则和基于 LLM 生成参考答案的 n-gram 统计来评分。这种评分需要既有效又多样的参考答案，而 LLM 在高棉语上未必能生成，因此我们研究了如何构建此类参考。我们发现经后训练的模型能给出比其基础版本更有效但更多样性更低的参考，且混合不同模型家族可在相同参考数量下提高多样性。使用来自九个模型家族的后训练模型的参考，该基准产生的模型排名在不同参考集间稳定，并与母语者的评分一致。这些发现为在其他低资源语言中构建无评判基准提供了指导。
translation.brief: 针对低资源语言中 LLM 评判者不可靠的问题，构建基于关键词规则和 n-gram 统计的无评判高棉语开放式生成基准。

papers.title: KLEAR: Knowledge-Matched LLM Evaluation in Korean across Application Requirements via Controlled Benchmark Transformation
papers.abstract: Existing Korean benchmarks for Large Language Models (LLMs) evaluate performance across diverse knowledge domains, but their accuracy scores cannot distinguish whether incorrect responses arise from a lack of required knowledge or a failure to apply that knowledge correctly. Our analysis of existing Korean benchmarks reveals that most questions can be answered through factual recall alone, while those demanding greater application also differ in required knowledge, making it difficult to isolate application ability. To address this, we introduce KLEAR, a framework that constructs knowledge-matched contrasts by varying application demand while preserving the required knowledge. During construction, KLEAR identifies the knowledge underlying each source question as an explicit anchor bundle to guide generation of questions requiring more complex application. Generated candidates then undergo automated and human validation, with iterative revision based on evaluation feedback. Experiments demonstrate that the resulting knowledge-matched sets largely satisfy the intended constraints, enabling controlled evaluation across diverse LLMs. These evaluations reveal that increasing application demand exposes failures that persist even when the required knowledge is provided.

translation.title: KLEAR: Knowledge-Matched LLM Evaluation in Korean across Application Requirements via Controlled Benchmark Transformation

To address this, we introduce KLEAR, a framework that constructs knowledge-matched contrasts by varying application demand while preserving the required knowledge. During construction, KLEAR identifies the knowledge underlying each source question as an explicit anchor bundle to guide generation of questions requiring more complex application. Generated candidates then undergo automated and human validation, with iterative revision based on evaluation feedback. Experiments demonstrate that the resulting knowledge-matched sets largely satisfy the intended constraints, enabling controlled evaluation across diverse LLMs. These evaluations reveal that increasing application demand exposes failures that persist even when the required knowledge is provided.

papers.title: RAG-Enhanced LLMs for Interactive Explainability in Clinical Decision Support Systems
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded in high-risks decision-making systems across domains such as healthcare, finance, and the judicial system. As reliance on predictive models grows, so does the demand for Explainable AI (XAI) to ensure transparency, trust, and interpretability. However, existing XAI approaches often fail to present explanations in a format accessible to domain experts, limiting their practical utility. Large Language Models (LLMs) have recently emerged as a bridge between complex models and end-users, offering natural language explanations. Yet, their use introduces new risks, including hallucinated outputs and lack of source traceability. To address these challenges, we propose a Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS) that not only combines standard predictive models with XAI techniques but also incorporates a Retrieval-Augmented Generation module as an interactive enhancer. This module grounds explanations in verified medical knowledge, reformulates technical outputs into a human-like format, and enables users-such as clinicians-to actively query the system. By fostering an interactive, human-in-the-loop environment, our approach empowers domain experts to explore model decisions, contextualize explanations, and build trust in AI-assisted diagnostics. The study concludes with preliminary experiments validating the proposed methodology.

papers.title: Controllable Molecule Generation via Sparse Representation Editing: An Interpretability-Driven Perspective
papers.abstract: Controllable molecule generation is crucial for diverse scientific applications, such as drug discovery and materials design. While large language models (LLMs) show great promise, their dense and entangled representations impede precise control over the generation of molecules with bespoke substructures or properties. To address this, we propose Sparse Representation Editing (SpaRE), an interpretability-driven framework for fine-grained and precise control in LLM-based molecule generation. The crux of SpaRE is to learn an overcomplete sparse feature space that disentangles LLM representations into a compact set of latent features corresponding to chemically meaningful concepts. Within this space, we can directly manipulate these concept-aligned latent features to achieve (1) local control, by generating target atoms and functional groups at specified positions; and (2) global control, by customizing the overall structural and physicochemical properties within defined ranges. In this way, our framework advances interpretability from post-hoc analysis to actionable generative control. Experiments show that SpaRE can generate chemically desirable molecules under complex constraints in real-world scenarios, while offering mechanistic insights for quantitative structure-property analysis. The code and demo are available at this https URL.

Within this space, we can directly manipulate these concept-aligned latent features to achieve (1) local control, by generating target atoms and functional groups at specified positions; and (2) global control, by customizing the overall structural and physicochemical properties within defined ranges. In this way, our framework advances interpretability from post-hoc analysis to actionable generative control. Experiments show that SpaRE can generate chemically desirable molecules under complex constraints in real-world scenarios, while offering mechanistic insights for quantitative structure-property analysis. The code and demo are available at this https URL.

papers.title: TwinHash: Two-Sided Object Identity Management for Time- and Energy-Efficient Agentic Workflows
papers.abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) services interleave large language model (LLM) generation with external tool execution, and increasingly rely on search-based workflows that repeatedly revisit shared reasoning states and computations. These patterns create substantial redundancy across tool outputs, LLM responses, and key-value (KV) prefixes, yet existing serving systems primarily optimize shared prompt prefixes, while naive input-keyed caching is unsafe when identical requests produce different outputs. We present TwinHash, a unified object management architecture that assigns each object an input-side hash key to recognize repeated requests and an output-side content fingerprint to validate and locate stored state, complemented by type-specific reuse guards that preserve correctness and response diversity. A software object identity table maintains reusable objects across requests and trajectories, while a hardware object placement table tracks their residency across hierarchical memory tiers so that evicted state can be retrieved rather than recomputed. Across seven agent frameworks and five benchmark suites, reuse follows workflow structure more than benchmark identity. TwinHash serves up to 81% of tool outputs wherever deterministic tool reads recur, and up to 92% of LLM responses in search-based frameworks. Retrieving an evicted KV-prefix from DRAM reduces TTFT by up to 5.6x on Qwen3-32B, with greater gains projected for larger dense models. Under search-based frameworks, TwinHash reduces end-to-end wall-clock time by up to 87% and measured task energy by up to 81% over a prefix-cached baseline, while a per-key serving cap controls the quality-reuse trade-off in adaptive search. These results demonstrate that unified identity, safety, and placement management can convert structural redundancy in emerging agentic workflows into substantial serving-efficiency gains.

papers.title: Zero-Query Transferable Pretend Benign Attacks with Amortized Online Generation for Cooperative Perception
papers.abstract: Cooperative perception enables an ego agent to acquire information from collaborators beyond its own sensors' reach. Yet, the most beneficial messages are often the hardest to verify from local observations. Pretend Benign (PB) exploits this asymmetry by targeting regions with weak local verifiability and applying multi-objective perturbations, making harmful feature changes appear to be benign assistance. However, PB is victim-dependent: selecting regions and optimizing perturbations require the victim model's architecture, parameters, and gradients, limiting transfer to unseen victims. A transferable attack must capture properties shared across cooperative detection models rather than those specific to one network. We address this by building a victim-agnostic attack from a heterogeneous ensemble of surrogate models and encoding its capabilities in a reusable dictionary to reduce per-message generation cost. Specifically, Transferable Pretend Benign (TrPB) transfers PB's region selection criterion and multi-objective perturbation strategy across heterogeneous surrogates to construct an offline attack. We further propose RT-TrPB, which encodes transferable regions and perturbation patterns into a region predictor and reusable perturbation dictionary, amortizing per-message attack generation. Experiments on widely used cooperative perception benchmarks show that RT-TrPB bypasses the consensus-based defenses ROBOSAC and FLD with success rates approaching 100% and generates each perturbation in under 56 ms. To counter PB-style attacks masquerading as benign collaboration, we also propose STTrust, which verifies received messages using spatial and temporal consistency and incorporates identity-level trust. STTrust detects over 90% of PB-style attacks and restores perception performance to near the attack-free level.

papers.title: Nudging Decision Models: Do Digital Nudges Steer Fast, Generation-Free AI Agents?
papers.abstract: LLM-based agents increasingly automate business and consumer tasks but are slow and expensive. Decision models, a new class that chooses among options without generating text, are far faster and less costly. Developers call them "System One models," referencing dual process theory. We ask whether such models can be steered by digital nudges online and whether, as the theory predicts, automatic nudges affect them more than reflective ones. We adapted an online shopping experiment, previously run with humans and LLM agents, to three decision models (Jev, Decision-1, d1). Across 600 runs per model, they chose a preselected default in 97.5-99.9% and a product with social influence information in 75-96% of choices, versus 47-49% in the control. All responded more strongly to the automatic nudge, the opposite of what has been reported for reasoning-capable LLM agents. We provide first evidence that non-generative decision models are susceptible to digital nudges in a System 1 pattern, implying agent-type-specific nudge effects.

translation.title: 引导决策模型：数字助推能否引导快速、无生成式AI智能体？
translation.abstract: 基于LLM的智能体日益自动化商业和消费任务，但速度慢且成本高。决策模型是一类无需生成文本即可在选项间做出选择的新模型，速度快得多且成本更低。开发者称其为"System One模型"，引用了双过程理论。我们探究此类模型能否被在线数字助推所引导，以及正如理论预测的那样，自动型助推是否比反思型助推对其影响更大。我们将一个此前在人类和LLM智能体上运行过的在线购物实验适配到三个决策模型（Jev、Decision-1、d1）上。在每模型600次运行中，它们在97.5-99.9%的情况下选择了预设默认项，在75-96%的选择中选择了带有社会影响信息的产品，而对照组为47-49%。所有模型对自动型助推的反应都更强，这与已报道的具备推理能力的LLM智能体的情况相反。我们首次提供了非生成式决策模型以System 1模式易受数字助推影响的证据，意味着助推效果因智能体类型而异。
translation.brief: 研究无生成式决策模型是否可被数字助推引导，通过将在线购物助推实验适配到三个决策模型上进行验证。

papers.title: FondueQA: A Benchmark for Evaluating Parametric Compensation in Multi-Hop QA
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) show remarkable performance based on parametric knowledge, i.e., their ability to recall facts and associations internalized in a model's weights. However, studying this capability on established multi-hop benchmarks may be complicated by benchmark contamination, as many of these benchmarks have been publicly available long enough to plausibly appear in modern pretraining corpora. As a result, correct answers under missing evidence may reflect either general parametric knowledge or memorization of benchmark-specific instances. To study how models use internal knowledge when retrieval evidence is incomplete, we introduce FondueQA, in which every required multi-hop fact is uniquely localized to a designated evidence document. This enables controlled document-level evidence ablations to study parametric compensation under incomplete retrieval. Our empirical evaluation reveals that parametric compensation strongly depends on both entity popularity and the structural role of missing evidence. Generally, models compensate more successfully for facts involving popular entities. On FondueQA, we show that bridging evidence can be more useful than the answer-bearing document itself. Moreover, models may recall a missing fact in isolation but fail to use it under partial evidence, particularly when the context contains plausible competing entities, which can reduce Exact Match by up to 15 percentage points.

translation.title: FondueQA：一个评估多跳问答中参数化补偿的基准
translation.abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）基于参数化知识（即模型权重中内化的记忆事实和关联的能力）展现出卓越性能。然而，在既有多跳基准上研究这一能力可能受基准污染的干扰，因为许多基准已公开足够久，很可能出现在现代预训练语料中。因此，在缺失证据情况下的正确答案可能反映的是通用参数化知识，或对基准特定实例的记忆。为研究模型在检索证据不完整时如何使用内部知识，我们提出FondueQA，其中每个所需的多跳事实都唯一地定位于指定的证据文档。这使得可以进行受控的文档级证据消融，以研究检索不完整时的参数化补偿。我们的实证评估表明，参数化补偿强烈依赖于实体流行度和缺失证据的结构角色。总体而言，模型对涉及流行实体的事实补偿更成功。在FondueQA上，我们显示桥接证据可能比包含答案的文档本身更有用。此外，模型可能孤立地回忆起缺失事实，但在部分证据下无法使用它，尤其当上下文包含看似合理的竞争实体时，这可使Exact Match降低多达15个百分点。
translation.brief: 提出FondueQA基准，通过将多跳事实唯一定位到证据文档并进行文档级证据消融，研究LLM在检索不完整时的参数化知识补偿。

papers.title: An Empirical Study of Issues in GPU Kernel Libraries for LLM Systems
papers.abstract: Behind the expanding use of large language models (LLMs) across application domains lies a growing dependence on specialized GPU kernel libraries. These libraries underpin the correctness and efficiency of training and inference across diverse GPU platforms, implementing attention, GEMM, quantization, and low-precision operators while managing tensor shapes, memory layouts, code generation, and hardware-specific dispatch. Problems at this layer can silently corrupt outputs, hang GPUs, prevent compilation, introduce deployment incompatibilities, or degrade performance, thereby reducing developer productivity and wasting expensive GPU resources. We present the first comprehensive empirical study of issues in GPU kernel libraries for LLM systems. We manually analyzed 300 high-quality GitHub issue reports, their discussions, and available fixes from seven representative libraries: FlashInfer, FlashAttention, Triton, CUTLASS, DeepGEMM, xFormers, and bitsandbytes. The analysis characterizes symptoms, root causes, fixes, and testing and debugging practices. Our main findings are: (1) 60.33% of the sampled issues originate in the Compiler and Build System or Runtime Environment dimensions, so validation must cover the deployment and execution stack, not just kernel code. (2) Kernel specialization imposes implicit correctness constraints on tensor shapes, metadata layouts, memory aliasing, and hardware resources. Violations can produce incorrect outputs or launch failures even for supported operations, highlighting the need for explicit contract validation and boundary-case testing. (3) Current testing and debugging practices are often insufficient for identifying low-precision numerical problems and hardware-specific execution failures. We outline research opportunities and tooling directions to support future LLM GPU kernel development.

translation.title: LLM系统GPU内核库问题的实证研究
translation.abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）在各应用领域不断扩展使用的背后，是对专用GPU内核库日益增长的依赖。这些库支撑着跨多样GPU平台的训练和推理的正确性与效率，实现注意力、GEMM、量化和低精度算子，同时管理张量形状、内存布局、代码生成和硬件特定分发。这一层的问题可能悄悄破坏输出、挂起GPU、阻止编译、引入部署不兼容或降低性能，从而降低开发者生产力并浪费昂贵的GPU资源。我们首次对LLM系统的GPU内核库问题进行了全面的实证研究。我们手动分析了来自七个代表性库（FlashInfer、FlashAttention、Triton、CUTLASS、DeepGEMM、xFormers和bitsandbytes）的300份高质量GitHub issue报告、其讨论及可用修复。该分析刻画了症状、根因、修复以及测试和调试实践。主要发现：(1) 60.33%的抽样问题源于编译器与构建系统或运行时环境维度，因此验证必须覆盖部署和执行栈，而不仅是内核代码。(2) 内核特化对张量形状、元数据布局、内存别名和硬件资源施加了隐式正确性约束，违反这些约束即使对受支持的操作也可能产生错误输出或启动失败，凸显了显式契约验证和边界用例测试的必要性。(3) 当前的测试和调试实践往往不足以识别低精度数值问题和硬件特定的执行失败。我们概述了支持未来LLM GPU内核开发的研究机会和工具方向。
translation.brief: 对七个GPU内核库的300个GitHub issue进行手动实证分析，刻画LLM系统内核库问题的症状、根因与修复模式。

papers.title: Ontology-Driven Control of Conversational Agents with a Use-Case for Job Interview Practice
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have been widely used as conversational agents in both domain-specific and open-domain situations. In domain-specific context, it is often necessary to adapt those LLMs to obtain conversations with desired characteristics, whether those apply at the level of each response (e.g. for tone or style) or more globally (i.e. at the level of a conversational strategy). Such adaptations are, however, generally realized in an ad hoc way, through specific, non-reusable, and non-transparent developments. In this paper, we propose an ontology-based approach to design conversational strategies that rely on the desired and measured characteristics of textual utterances in the conversation. Through a use case related to job interview practice, we show how this approach can be used to control LLMs to follow the strategy defined in the ontology. To this end, we automatically fine-tune the LLM to improve its compliance with ontologically-defined conversation characteristics. Our results show that training the LLM from formally defined concepts effectively enhances alignment with the requested characteristics. Hence, this work demonstrates how ontology-guided conversation control can be achieved while taking into account multiple, concurrent conversation aspects that are formally and transparently defined.

translation.title: 基于本体的对话智能体控制：以求职面试练习为用例
translation.abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）已被广泛用作领域特定和开放域场景中的对话智能体。在领域特定情境下，通常需要适配这些LLM以获得具有期望特征的对话，无论这些特征作用于每条回复层面（如语气或风格）还是更全局的层面（即对话策略层面）。然而，此类适配通常以临时方式实现，通过特定的、不可复用且不透明的开发。本文提出一种基于本体的方法来设计对话策略，该策略依赖于对话中文本话语的期望特征和实测特征。通过一个求职面试练习的用例，我们展示了如何使用该方法控制LLM遵循本体中定义的策略。为此，我们自动微调LLM以提高其对本体定义的对话特征的遵从度。结果表明，从形式化定义的概念训练LLM有效增强了对所请求特征的对齐。因此，这项工作展示了如何在形式化且透明地定义多个并发对话方面的同时实现本体引导的对话控制。
translation.brief: 提出基于本体的对话策略设计方法，通过自动微调LLM使其遵从本体形式化定义的对话特征，并以求职面试练习为用例验证。

papers.title: AutoRefine: Auto-Calibrating Code Judges from Workflow Outcomes
papers.abstract: LLM judges increasingly serve as quality gates for code changes that have no test oracle, but a judge prompt must be calibrated for its task and recalibrated as the system it judges evolves, while hand labels for the calibration are resource intensive and go stale. Development workflows emit outcome labels for free (tests pass or fail, changes land or are abandoned), but these labels are noisy. We present AutoRefine, a loop that rewrites a deployable judge's prompt to reproduce outcome labels, with an informed teacher that sees the judge's input plus the outcome, explains each label it keeps, and abstains when the outcome cannot be explained from what the judge sees. On a held-out dataset with an execution oracle, calibration raised chance-corrected agreement (Scott's $\pi$) from 0.36 to 0.60. On a deployed agent's outcome labels, with 25\% flipped at random to introduce noise, the teacher set aside flipped \textsc{fail} labels at more than twice the rate of genuine ones, cutting overall label noise from 25\% to 20\%. Recalibrating that agent's judge using AutoRefine raised its agreement with merge/abandon outcomes on 17 independently held-out diffs from the current workflow ($\pi$ 0.16 to 0.51); on 16 diffs from older workflows, the previous judge stayed ahead, illustrating the need for recalibration as the agent evolves. By abstaining, the teacher not only removes noisy labels but also flags changes whose outcome the judge's input cannot explain, telling a team when a judge needs better inputs rather than a better prompt.

translation.title: AutoRefine：从工作流结果自动校准代码评判器
translation.abstract: LLM评判器日益充当无测试oracle的代码变更的质量门，但评判器提示必须针对其任务进行校准，并随其评判系统的演进而重新校准，而用于校准的人工标注资源密集且会过时。开发工作流免费产生结果标签（测试通过或失败、变更合入或被放弃），但这些标签有噪声。我们提出AutoRefine，一个重写可部署评判器提示以复现结果标签的循环，其中包含一个知情的教师：它能看到评判器的输入加上结果，解释其保留的每个标签，并在无法从评判器所见内容解释结果时弃权。在一个带执行oracle的留出数据集上，校准将机会校正一致性（Scott's $\pi$）从0.36提升到0.60。在一个已部署智能体的结果标签上（随机翻转25%以引入噪声），教师搁置被翻转的FAIL标签的比率是真实标签的两倍以上，将整体标签噪声从25%降至20%。使用AutoRefine重新校准该智能体的评判器，将其在17个来自当前工作流的独立留出diff上与合入/放弃结果的一致性从$\pi$ 0.16提升到0.51；而在16个来自旧工作流的diff上，旧评判器仍保持领先，说明随智能体演进需要重新校准。通过弃权，教师不仅去除噪声标签，还标记出评判器输入无法解释其结果的变更，告诉团队何时评判器需要更好的输入而非更好的提示。
translation.brief: 提出AutoRefine循环，利用开发工作流免费产生的结果标签自动重写LLM评判器提示，并通过知情教师过滤噪声标签实现持续校准。

papers.title: Towards an Autonomous AI Steward for Large-Scale Physics Experiments: Integrating Causal Diagnostics, RAG, and Conformal Prediction
papers.abstract: Long-term particle physics experiments face critical operational challenges: monitoring non-stationary machine data streams and preserving tacit expert knowledge. We present the "Helmholtz Co-Pilot," a hybrid Multi-Agent System (MAS) acting as an autonomous experiment steward. The system can be triggered interactively by human operators or autonomously by an asynchronous causal diagnostics engine that runs independently of the MAS reasoning core. Continuously monitoring live hardware streams such as data acquisition and slow control, this engine performs dynamic causal discovery to trace cascading alarms back to their root causes and applies adaptive model selection to keep forecasts reliable across shifting machine states; upon detecting an anomaly, it hands a structured diagnostic report to the MAS. The reasoning layer itself relies on a high-throughput C++ core and a Python edge architecture orchestrating a directed acyclic graph (DAG) of specialized ReAct workers. It integrates a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) backbone for institutional memory and leverages conformal prediction to bound its evidence-based recommendations with mathematical coverage guarantees. This extended abstract outlines the architecture, the integration of software-enforced Human-in-the-Loop (HitL) guardrails, and ongoing shadow-testing within the KATRIN experiment.

papers.title: Wake 5: A Python Framework for Solidity Testing, Fuzzing, and Static Analysis
papers.abstract: Smart-contract fuzzers differ by an order of magnitude in throughput and by design in how they construct inputs, yet published comparisons rarely separate the two. We present Wake 5, an open-source Python framework for Solidity testing, fuzzing and static analysis, and use it to locate the binding constraint of stateful smart-contract fuzzing. Wake 5 replaces the JSON-RPC connection to an external node with an in-process EVM (revm) and exposes its static analysis to language-model agents through a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server. On the Daedaluzz maze benchmark (153 reachable assertions, guard constants below 2^32), Wake 5 executes 29,931 transactions per second, on par with Foundry (30,186) and 11.5x faster than Echidna (2,600). In eight-hour campaigns, however, the three tools plateau at medians of 75, 71 and 70 assertions, and their union reaches 93. We show that Wake's integer generator places 51% of its probability mass below 2^32 and that, once shallow assertions are exhausted, the generator prior rather than throughput bounds every tool. A harness written by a language-model agent, which derives inputs with a constraint solver, reached all 153 assertions in each of five campaigns executed by Wake, in 33 to 79 minutes. A complementary ablation in an agentic audit of a production Go codebase found that static-analysis tools improved recall for none of three models, raised precision for all three, and increased language-model cost by up to 12.7%. We discuss correlated oracles and non-deterministic completion, and argue that the fuzzer's role is shifting from search to execution.
